web.title: Taash Housie: Diwali Card Kitty Party Game Rules and Twists
web.description: Taash Housie is a Diwali kitty party game where 5 playing cards are your Housie ticket and a Joker makes everyone pass a card. Rules, steps, twists, FAQs.
web.intro: Taash Housie is a Diwali kitty party game that mixes taash (playing cards) with Housie: each lady gets 5 cards face up as her ticket, the host flips cards from a second deck and calls them out, and whoever holds a called card turns it face down. The first lady to turn all 5 cards face down shouts "Diwali!" and wins. The crazy twist is the Joker: whenever the host flips one, every lady must pass one of her open cards to the lady on her right. It is perfect for a Diwali taash night with no money involved, works for 8 to 20 ladies and takes 10 to 15 minutes.
materials: Ticket decks: one deck of playing cards for every 10 ladies, Jokers taken out
One calling deck for the host, with all the Jokers from every deck shuffled in (4 to 6 Jokers works well)
A table, a durrie or any flat space where every lady can lay out 5 cards
One host to flip and call the cards
A small prize like a toffee, a chocolate or a box of mithai
steps: Take the Jokers out of the ticket decks and shuffle them into the host's calling deck.
Deal 5 cards from the ticket decks to every lady. She lays them face up in front of her: this is her Housie ticket.
The host flips the calling deck one card at a time and calls it out loud in Hindi or English, for example "Paan ki satti" for the 7 of hearts.
Every called card is placed face up in a line in the middle so everyone can check what has already been called.
Any lady holding the called card turns it face down. With two ticket decks, two ladies can hold the same card and both turn it down.
When the host flips a Joker, every lady passes one of her open (face up) cards to the lady on her right at the same time. If the card you receive was already called, turn it down at once.
The first lady with all 5 cards face down shouts "Diwali!". The host checks her cards against the called line and she wins the prize.
rules: A lady who turns down a wrong card must keep her ticket frozen for the next 3 calls.
Only open cards can be passed on a Joker. A face down card passed by mistake is turned face up again.
A false "Diwali!" call costs one card: turn one of your face down cards back up.
No money or betting at all. The prize is a toffee, chocolate or mithai.
The first lady with all 5 cards face down is the Taash Queen.
variations: Second Joker rule: after the first Joker, every new Joker changes direction, so cards go to the left next time.
Mute round: the host shows the card only with hand signs and faces, no words.
Housie prizes: a small prize for the first lady with 3 cards down and the big prize for the full house of 5.
tips: Use the Hindi card names (Paan, Eent, Hukum, Chidi; Ekka, Badshah, Begum, Ghulam) to make the calling more fun.
Keep the line of called cards in the middle tidy so passed cards can be checked quickly.
For older ladies or big groups, let each lady sit with her 5 cards on a plate or tray so they do not slide.
If the game runs long, the host can call two cards at a time near the end.

faq.q: How many players do you need for Taash Housie?
faq.a: It works best with 8 to 20 ladies. Use one ticket deck for every 10 ladies plus one calling deck for the host.

faq.q: What do you need to play Taash Housie?
faq.a: Just playing cards, a host and a small prize. No Housie tickets, pens or printouts are needed.

faq.q: Is Taash Housie a good Diwali kitty party game?
faq.a: Yes. Taash is a Diwali tradition, and this version keeps the card party fun without any money or gambling, so everyone can play.

faq.q: What happens when a Joker comes in Taash Housie?
faq.a: Everyone passes one open card to the lady on her right. A lady who was close to winning can suddenly get a fresh card to wait for.

faq.q: How long does a game of Taash Housie take?
faq.a: About 10 to 15 minutes for one full house. You can play 2 or 3 rounds in a kitty.
